requirements: Root separately establishes native closure of both first original owner/timeout processes and absence of both canonical owner operation leaves and worker output leaves.
Create only the empty exact amendment-root/owners parent; operation owner leaves and preflight worker output leaves are still created exclusively by the unchanged owner/worker.
Do not run unchanged operator issue, restart the phase, edit approval, renew600 seconds, shorten/relabel original history, alter scientific inputs/argv, or repeat a started worker.

If original CPU clock is stale, preserve and hash the old remote canonical CPU-release bytes before an explicitly recorded replacement; preserve original local attempt1 controls and receipts unchanged.

Fresh CPU controls may change only issued_utc, clock_sample, invocation_origin_utc, remaining_shared_amendment_seconds, hard_deadline_monotonic_ns and derived CPU byte hash/bootstrap literal bindings; use the SAME phase stop, work_stop E-15, cleanup E-5, phase/approval/core/source/input/command/output bindings.
Owner requires canonical remote controls/{operation}.cpu_release.json; attempt2 is a separate local evidence namespace, not a new remote control/output path.

Fresh host sample must pass <=300-second age, exact boot, UTC/monotonic consistency and root/host <=5-second checks. Derive hard deadline from fresh sample plus remaining-to-original-stop minus5 seconds; do not extend effective deadline.
Original mode/core release has no independent300-second staleness check and can remain byte-identical; mode issuance must precede new CPU issuance and retain the same approved phase start/stop.
Complete original attempt2 tool exit, native closure, input/output capture and product review must fit inside the unchanged phase. Source compatibility alone does not establish time feasibility.
